newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish one-day deposits end year at 21.5 percent.
newsitem.headline: Polish one-day deposits end year at 21.5 percent.

text.p: The Polish one-day deposit rates stabilised around 21.5 percent gradually loosing steam ahead of the New Year Holiday and because of the changeover in the accounts coming in force from the start of 1997, dealers said.
They said that few market players would have predicted such rates several months ago when one-day deposits traded around 19 percent.
"Looking back to bank's anticipations three, four-months ago this level is rather puzzling because one should have expected rates to stay around 19 percent," said Krzysztof Bury from Kredyt Bank SA.

Dealers said the year-end rise in rates, however surprising, was justified by a recent credit boom. "This is optimistic that rates follow the situation, when the symptoms of overheating appear," said dealer at a Polish bank.
Overnight rates were quoted at 21.30/21.70 percent against opening's 21.00/22.00 percent, tomorrow/next rates were at 21.50/21.75 percent against opening's 21.00/22.00 percent.

The NBP sold 300 million zlotys of its 182-day NBP-bills, the average rate rose 0.62 point to 21.95 percent against last week's 26-week T-bill primary average yield of 19.30 percent and the secondary market's 20.00/19.25 percent.

Dealers said such a wide yield spread between two similar instruments illustrated conflicting pressures from the central bank and the finance ministry, with the bank keen on driving rates high to control money supply and the ministry striving to depress rates to reduce the cost of deficit financing.

"There is a clear conflict of interest between the central bank which draws rates up and the finance ministry, which tries to push it the other way," said Wojciech Labryga from Bank Slaski SA. -- Krzysztof Wojcik +48 22 653 9700
